texts.error.boot_rom: This game needs the Lynx's boot ROM, %1. Add it to the project's firmware.

texts.error.no_file: No game file is in the project.
texts.error.no_file_player: No game for player %1's Lynx is in the project.
texts.error.not_loaded: Gearlynx could not load '%1' as a Lynx game.

texts.firmware.lynxboot_img.about: The 512 bytes of code a Lynx runs when it is switched on. It decrypts and starts the cartridge, so every cartridge needs it. A BS93 program (.o) does not.
texts.setting.allowopposite.about: Lets Up and Down, or Left and Right, reach the game together, which a real joystick cannot do. When off, the direction held last frame wins, else Up or Left. It changes what the game reads, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.eeprom.about: The EEPROM chip a cartridge keeps its saved games in, if it has one. Automatic takes the one the game's header or Gearlynx's list of games names. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.fastsprites.about: Draws sprites with Gearlynx's older, faster method instead of the exact one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: One Lynx, or two to four Lynxes joined by the ComLynx cable, each with its own game and its own player. Linked Lynxes are one machine: their screens side by side, their sounds together. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.model.about: Which Lynx runs the game: the first model or the Lynx II. Automatic takes the one the game's header asks for, or else the Lynx II. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The number that decides what the processor and some of the chips hold when the console is switched on. On a real Lynx they hold whatever was left there. With this number fixed, the same project always starts the same way, and a movie records the number it used.
texts.setting.rotation.about: Some games are played with the Lynx held on its side. This turns the picture, and the joystick with it, so that Up stays up. Automatic does what the game's header or Gearlynx's list of games says. It changes how the joystick is read, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.slot.game.help: The Lynx game: a cartridge as a .lnx file (with its header) or a .lyx file (without one), or a BS93 program (.o), the format homebrew is sent to a Lynx in.
texts.slot.game2.help: The game of the Lynx player 2 plays on a link machine. The same game as the others' is fine.
texts.slot.game3.help: The game of the Lynx player 3 plays on a link machine. The same game as the others' is fine.
texts.slot.game4.help: The game of the Lynx player 4 plays on a link machine. The same game as the others' is fine.
texts.slot.savedata.help: Optional: what the cartridge's EEPROM holds at the start, a .sav file as Export Save Data writes it. Leave it empty to start with an empty EEPROM.
texts.slot.savedata2.help: Optional: what the EEPROM of Lynx 2's cartridge holds at the start, a .sav file as Export Save Data writes it.
texts.slot.savedata3.help: Optional: what the EEPROM of Lynx 3's cartridge holds at the start, a .sav file as Export Save Data writes it.
texts.slot.savedata4.help: Optional: what the EEPROM of Lynx 4's cartridge holds at the start, a .sav file as Export Save Data writes it.
